source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 4 (Climate).

sections.heading: 1. India's Climate — the Monsoon Type
points: India has a **tropical monsoon climate** ('monsoon' from Arabic 'mausim' = season); marked by **seasonal reversal of winds**.
Great **regional variations** in temperature and rainfall (e.g. Mawsynram = wettest, Thar = driest).

sections.heading: 2. Factors Controlling Climate
points: **Latitude** (Tropic of Cancer divides India into tropical south and subtropical north).
**Altitude** (Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds, keeping India warmer).
**Pressure and winds** (monsoon circulation), **distance from the sea (continentality)**, **relief**, and **ocean currents**.
The **Himalayas** act as a climatic barrier; the **jet streams** and **El Niño (ENSO)** also affect the monsoon.

sections.heading: 3. The Monsoon Mechanism
points: **Differential heating** of land and sea; the **ITCZ** (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone) shifts north in summer, drawing in moist winds.
**Southwest monsoon (June–September)** — 'burst of monsoon'; enters as **Arabian Sea branch** and **Bay of Bengal branch**; brings most of India's rain.
**Northeast (retreating) monsoon (Oct–Nov)** — winds reverse; brings rain to the **Tamil Nadu (Coromandel) coast**.
**Jet streams** (subtropical westerly and tropical easterly), the **Tibetan Plateau heating**, and **El Niño/La Niña** influence monsoon strength.

sections.heading: 4. Seasons of India
points: **Cold weather (winter, Dec–Feb)** — dry NE winds; **western disturbances** bring rain to the northwest.
**Hot weather (summer, Mar–May)** — high temperatures; local storms: **loo** (hot wind), **Kalbaisakhi** (Bengal), **mango showers** (Kerala/Karnataka).
**Southwest monsoon (rainy, June–Sept)** — main rainy season.
**Retreating monsoon (Oct–Nov)** — autumn; October heat; cyclones on the east coast.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Monsoon = seasonal reversal of winds ('mausim' = season).
SW monsoon (June–Sept) = main rainy season; two branches (Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal).
NE (retreating) monsoon brings rain to Tamil Nadu (Coromandel coast).
Mawsynram/Cherrapunji = wettest; western disturbances bring winter rain to the NW.
El Niño weakens the monsoon; jet streams affect its onset.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Tamil Nadu gets most rain from the NORTHEAST (retreating) monsoon** (Oct–Nov).
**Western disturbances** bring **winter** rain to NW India.
**Mango showers** and **Kalbaisakhi** are **pre-monsoon** (summer) storms.
**El Niño weakens** the Indian monsoon.
